sections.title: What is a Skeleton?
points: A skeleton is the supportive framework of bones or hard tissues in an organism.
It is a living tissue because it has a blood supply, nerves, and living cells.
Bones are the hardest tissues in the body and need proper feeding to stay healthy.
The primary minerals that make bones strong are Calcium and Phosphorus.

sections.title: 1. Exo-skeleton (Outer Support)
points: Definition: Hard tissues found outside the flesh/body.
Found in: Insects and Arthropods.
Examples: Cockroaches, Grasshoppers, Crickets, Houseflies, Mosquitoes, Spiders, Scorpions, Crabs, Lobsters, Centipedes, and Millipedes.
Special Case: A Tortoise has an exo-skeleton (shell) but also an endo-skeleton (internal bones).
Functions: Provides protection to soft internal organs and supports the body.

sections.title: Growth: Ecdysis / Moulting
points: Animals with exo-skeletons cannot grow continuously because their 'shell' is rigid.
Ecdysis (Moulting): The process of shedding the old outer layer to form a new, larger one.
This allows the animal to increase in size.

sections.title: 2. Hydrostatic Skeleton (Liquid Support)
points: Definition: The body is filled with liquid under pressure within a thin membrane.
Movement: They use the pressure of the fluid and surrounding muscles to change shape and move.
Examples: Earthworms, Slugs, Snails, Maggots, Caterpillars, Jellyfish, Starfish, Sea Urchins, and Octopuses.

sections.title: 3. Endo-skeleton (Inner Support)
points: Definition: Hard tissues (bones and cartilage) found inside the flesh.
Found in: All Vertebrates (animals with backbones).
Examples: Humans (Man), Cows, Goats, Dogs, Lions, Birds, Fish, Frogs (Amphibians), and Snakes (Reptiles).
Growth: Unlike insects, vertebrates grow continuously without shedding.

sections.title: General Functions of the Skeleton
points: Shape: Gives the body its specific framework.
Support: Supports the soft parts of the body so we can stand/sit.
Protection: Protects delicate organs (e.g., Skull protects the Brain).
Blood Manufacture: The Bone Marrow produces red and white blood cells.
Movement: Provides surfaces for Muscles to attach at the joints.
Storage: Acts as a bank for minerals like Calcium.

sections.text: Remember: Sharks are vertebrates but their skeleton is made of Cartilage, not hard bone! Also, Babies have over 300 bones/cartilages, which fuse into 206 bones in adults.

cards.fact: The periodic shedding of the exoskeleton to allow the animal to grow.
cards.mnemonic: Think of 'Exit' - The insect exits its old skin to grow bigger!

cards.fact: Support provided by fluid under pressure in soft-bodied animals.
cards.mnemonic: Hydro = Water. Like a water-filled balloon that holds its shape!

cards.fact: Bones are alive; they grow, need food (minerals), and have nerves to feel pain.
cards.mnemonic: Bones aren't stones! They have Blood and Breathing cells.
